subject: Learning Methods
title: Atomic Notes
description: A quick win: understand Atomic Notes.

hook.text: His notes were sprawling pages covering multiple topics each. Finding a specific idea meant rereading everything.

buildup.text: Atomic notes contain exactly one idea per note. They are small, self-contained, and independently meaningful.

discovery.text: Small notes can be linked, rearranged, and recombined. Large notes are rigid. Atomicity enables flexibility.

twist.text: Splitting into atomic notes feels tedious at first. But the investment pays off when you need to find or connect ideas.

climax.text: Each note should answer: what is this one idea? Give it a clear title that could stand alone in a search result.

punchline.text: One idea, one note. Small pieces connect freely.

quiz.question: Why are atomic notes more useful over time than long multi-topic notes?
options: They can be individually linked, found, and recombined flexibly
They are faster to write during lectures
